label: Organisation profile
summary: Asked once per organisation and reused by every framework's onboarding. A framework only asks for what is specific to it and picks rows from this profile (sites, systems, third parties, data types) by id.

source.ref: Certification-body application forms (headcount, sites, shifts, outsourcing), HITRUST scope forms, SOC 2 system description

fields.label: Legal entity
fields.note: The name that appears on a certificate, an attestation report or a regulator filing. Kept in Administration > Organization; this is the same value.

fields.label: Structure
fields.note: Decides whether one scope covers one company or several, and who signs for the group.

fields.label: Industry
fields.note: Sector decides which regulators and which framework variants apply (for example NIS2 annex sectors, SAMA member categories).

fields.label: Company size
fields.note: Band of staff. The exact figures are in Headcount; several rules (NIS2, DORA proportionality, NCA private-sector tiers) depend on size.

fields.label: Geography
fields.note: Where the organisation operates, in one word. Countries are listed under Jurisdictions.

fields.label: Headcount
fields.note: All staff including contractors and freelancers. Certification bodies use it to set audit time and regulators use it for size tests.

fields.label: Revenue
fields.note: Annual turnover. Needed for size classes (NIS2, SOX filer status, NCA private-sector tiers). A rough figure is fine.

fields.label: Currency
fields.note: Currency of the revenue figure.

fields.label: Legal entities
fields.note: Every company that could be in the scope of a framework: parent, subsidiaries, branches. A framework scope later picks from this list.

fields.label: Sites
fields.note: Permanent and temporary sites with their staff and shifts. Certification bodies ask for exactly this to plan audits; HITRUST needs every facility that hosts an in-scope system.

fields.label: Units
fields.note: Departments and sub-departments come from Governance > Settings > Departments. A framework scope picks the units it covers; define at least one first.

source.ref: Regulator applicability rules, certification-body application forms (prior certificates), card-brand and customer requirements

fields.label: Jurisdictions
fields.note: Countries where the organisation is established, serves customers or holds data of residents. Territorial reach (GDPR Art. 3, PDPL, NIS2 Art. 26) starts here.

fields.label: Regulatory scope
fields.note: A short phrase for the regime the organisation says it is under (kept in Administration > Organization).

fields.label: Regulators
fields.note: Every authority that licenses, supervises or receives reports from the organisation. Applicability of most regulator frameworks follows from this list.

fields.label: No regulator
fields.note: Tick when no authority supervises the organisation, so an empty list is a decision and not an omission.

fields.label: Certifications
fields.note: Certificates and attestations held today, with validity. Certification bodies ask for prior certificates, transfers and expiry dates.

fields.label: No certifications
fields.note: Tick when the organisation holds no certificate or attestation yet.

fields.label: Audit history
fields.note: The last audits, inspections and reports with their date and result. Assessors read previous findings first; open findings often have to be closed before a new audit.

fields.label: No audits yet
fields.note: Tick when the organisation has never been audited.

fields.label: Obligations
fields.note: Frameworks someone requires of the organisation: a regulator, a customer contract, an acquirer, a parent company, or its own decision. Feeds which frameworks to onboard first.

source.ref: Records of processing (GDPR Art. 30), PCI DSS account-data flows and inventory, HIPAA ePHI inventory, NCA ECC asset inventory and classification, ISO/IEC 27001 cl. 4.3 interfaces

fields.label: Classification
fields.note: Name and levels of the data classification scheme in use, for example Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted. NCA, SAMA, QCB, NDMO and ISO all start from it.

fields.label: Data types
fields.note: The kinds of data held, how they are classified and how much. Drives personal-data, card-data, health-data and CUI applicability.

fields.label: Special environments
fields.note: Triggers that switch whole frameworks on: PCI DSS, SWIFT CSCF, OT controls, ISO 42001 and NIST AI RMF, HIPAA, NIST 800-171, CCC, NCA ECC.

fields.label: Hosting
fields.note: Where systems run. Cloud use switches on cloud rules (NCA CCC, SBP and QCB cloud frameworks, SAMA 3.4.3, CSA CCM).

fields.label: Key systems
fields.note: The applications and infrastructure that carry the business, picked from the asset library. Every framework scope picks a subset of these.

fields.label: Asset inventory
fields.note: CIS Controls, NCA ECC and CMMC all start from an inventory. Partial is accepted, but frameworks that need it will say so.

fields.label: Third parties
fields.note: Cloud, SaaS, outsourced and processor relationships that touch in-scope systems or data. DORA registers, SBP and QCB cloud registers, PCI TPSP lists and SOC 2 subservice lists all pick from here.

fields.label: No third parties
fields.note: Tick when nothing is outsourced or hosted by others.

fields.label: Data flows
fields.note: Whether data flows between systems and parties are drawn. PCI DSS, GDPR records and HIPAA all need them; a first pass is enough to start.

fields.label: Flow diagram
fields.note: Where the diagram lives (document title or link).

fields.label: Data subjects
fields.note: Countries whose residents' personal data is processed. Decides GDPR, PDPL and similar reach.

source.ref: ISO/IEC 27001 cl. 5.3 and 6.1.2, NIST CSF 2.0 GV.RM and GV.RR, regulator governance requirements (NCA ECC 1-2, SAMA 3.1.1, QCB 1.2, MAS TRM 3.1)

fields.label: Risk appetite
fields.note: Where the board stands on risk. Frameworks use it to set priorities and tolerances; Not defined is allowed but is flagged.

fields.label: Approval
fields.note: Who approved the risk appetite statement.

fields.label: Tolerance notes
fields.note: Tolerances in the organisation's own words, for example maximum tolerable outage or loss.

fields.label: Risk method
fields.note: The method used to assess risk. ISO 27001 6.1.2 and the CSF both expect one to be fixed first.

fields.label: Risk register
fields.note: Whether risks are kept in a register (the Risk Management module counts).

fields.label: Security policy
fields.note: Top-level information security policy status. Most certifications expect it approved by top management.

fields.label: Cyber reports to
fields.note: Who the security function reports to. NCA, SAMA and QCB require it to be independent of IT.

fields.label: Cyber committee
fields.note: Name of the committee that oversees cyber and information security, if any.

fields.label: Sponsor
fields.note: The executive who owns the compliance programme and signs scope and approvals. ISO 33002-style assessments and most certification bodies start from a named sponsor.

fields.label: Compliance lead
fields.note: The person who runs onboarding day to day and answers the assessor.

fields.label: CISO
fields.note: Head of information security (an outsourced CISO is allowed: enter their name and organisation).

fields.label: DPO
fields.note: Data protection officer, where one is appointed or required.

fields.label: CIO
fields.note: Head of IT or technology.

fields.label: Head of risk
fields.note: Owner of enterprise risk management.

fields.label: Internal audit
fields.note: Head of internal audit. Assessors check that audit is independent of the people who run the controls.

fields.label: Legal counsel
fields.note: Who answers legal and contractual questions (legal register, contracts).

fields.label: Other contacts
fields.note: Other roles frameworks ask for, such as an outsourced DPO, a QSA liaison or an authorised official.

checks.label: Regulators listed, or none declared
checks.hint: List the authorities, or tick that there are none.

checks.label: Certifications listed, or none declared
checks.hint: List what is held today, or tick that nothing is.

checks.label: Previous audits listed, or none declared
checks.hint: List the last audits with their result, or tick that none exist.

checks.label: Third parties listed, or none declared
checks.hint: List cloud, SaaS and outsourced services, or tick that there are none.

checks.label: At least one department defined
checks.hint: Add departments in Governance > Settings so frameworks can pick units.

checks.label: Sponsor and compliance lead are different people
checks.hint: An executive signs; someone else runs the work.

checks.label: Risk appetite defined
checks.hint: Frameworks set priorities from the board's appetite.
